summary.en: Romeo and Juliet meet at Friar Lawrence's cell, and he marries them in secret.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
So smile the heavens upon this holy act
That after-hours with sorrow chide us not.

sentences.en: May heaven smile on this holy act.
May it not cause us sorrow later.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Amen, amen, but come what sorrow can,
It cannot countervail the exchange of joy
That one short minute gives me in her sight.
Do thou but close our hands with holy words,
Then love-devouring death do what he dare,
It is enough I may but call her mine.

sentences.en: Amen, amen.
Whatever sorrow may come, it cannot outweigh the joy that one short minute with her gives me.
Just join our hands with holy words.
Then let death do what it dares.
It is enough that I can call her mine.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
These violent delights have violent ends,
And in their triumph die; like fire and powder,
Which as they kiss consume. The sweetest honey
Is loathsome in his own deliciousness,
And in the taste confounds the appetite.
Therefore love moderately: long love doth so;
Too swift arrives as tardy as too slow.

sentences.en: These violent delights have violent ends and die in their triumph.
They are like fire and gunpowder, which explode as they kiss.
Even the sweetest honey becomes sickening when you have too much.
Its taste ruins the appetite, so love moderately.
That is how love lasts.
Going too fast gets you there as late as going too slow.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Here comes the lady. O, so light a foot
Will ne’er wear out the everlasting flint.
A lover may bestride the gossamers
That idles in the wanton summer air
And yet not fall; so light is vanity.

sentences.en: Here comes the lady.
Her step is so light it would never wear down the hard stone path.
A lover could walk on the spider threads that float in the summer air and not fall.
Earthly joy is that light.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Good even to my ghostly confessor.

sentences.en: Good evening, Father.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: Romeo shall thank thee, daughter, for us both.

sentences.en: Romeo will thank you, daughter, for both of us.

speaker: JULIET
raw: As much to him, else is his thanks too much.

sentences.en: Then I give him the same thanks, or his thanks would be too much.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Ah, Juliet, if the measure of thy joy
Be heap’d like mine, and that thy skill be more
To blazon it, then sweeten with thy breath
This neighbour air, and let rich music’s tongue
Unfold the imagin’d happiness that both
Receive in either by this dear encounter.

sentences.en: Ah, Juliet.
Your joy may be as great as mine, and you may be better at showing it.
Then sweeten this air with your breath.
Let the music of rich words tell our story.
Let it show the happiness we both feel from this dear meeting.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Conceit more rich in matter than in words,
Brags of his substance, not of ornament.
They are but beggars that can count their worth;
But my true love is grown to such excess,
I cannot sum up sum of half my wealth.

sentences.en: My feelings are richer in meaning than in words.
They show my true feelings instead of just using fancy words.
Only beggars can count how much they have.
But my true love has grown so rich that I cannot count even half of my wealth.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Come, come with me, and we will make short work,
For, by your leaves, you shall not stay alone
Till holy church incorporate two in one.

sentences.en: Come with me now.
We will finish this quickly.
You will not be left alone together until the church joins you two as one.
